title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 18. The Prelude to Sannyasa
html:
In a dream the Lord is given the mantra of sannyasa; Keshava Bharati comes to Navadvipa; the Lord consoles Srivasa, instructs Murari, and in Kantakanagara accepts sannyasa. End of the second prakrama

Verse 1

ततः कियद्दिने प्राह भगवान्कार्यमानुषः।
स्वप्ने दृष्टो मया कश्चिदागत्य ब्राह्मणोत्तमः॥१॥

tataḥ kiyaddine prāha bhagavānkāryamānuṣaḥ|
svapne dṛṣṭo mayā kaścidāgatya brāhmaṇottamaḥ||1||

tatah — then; kiyat-dine — after some days; praha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; karya-manushah — human for the sake of (His) task; svapne — in a dream; drishtah — was seen; maya — by Me; kashchit — a certain; agatya — coming; brahmana-uttamah — excellent brahmana.

1Some days later Bhagavan, who for the sake of His mission was playing the part of a man, said, "I dreamt that a certain excellent brahmana came to Me,

Verse 2

सन्न्यासमन्त्रं मत्कर्णे कथयामास सुस्मितः।
तच्छ्रुत्वा व्यथितो रात्रौ दिवा चाहं विरोदिमि॥२॥

sannyāsamantraṁ matkarṇe kathayāmāsa susmitaḥ|
tacchrutvā vyathito rātrau divā cāhaṁ virodimi||2||

sannyasa-mantram — the mantra of sannyasa; mat-karne — into My ear; kathayam asa — spoke; su-smitah — smiling sweetly; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; vyathitah — pained; ratrau — by night; diva — by day; cha — and; aham — I; virodimi — weep.

2and, smiling sweetly, spoke the mantra of sannyasa into My ear. Since hearing it I have been grieving, weeping by night and by day.

Verse 3

कथं प्रियं हरिं नाथं त्यक्त्वान्यदुचितं मम।
मुरारिः प्राह तच्छ्रुत्वा तन्मन्त्रे भगवान्स्वयम्॥३॥

kathaṁ priyaṁ hariṁ nāthaṁ tyaktvānyaducitaṁ mama|
murāriḥ prāha tacchrutvā tanmantre bhagavānsvayam||3||

katham — how; priyam — the dear; harim — Hari; natham — the Lord; tyaktva — abandoning; anyat — something else; uchitam — is fitting; mama — for Me; murarih — Murari; praha — said; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; tat-mantre — in that mantra; bhagavan — Bhagavan; svayam — Himself.

3How can I abandon dear Hari, My Lord? What else could befit Me?" Hearing this, Murari said, "In that mantra is Bhagavan Himself.

Verse 4

षष्ठीसमासं मनसा विचिन्त्य त्वं सुखी भव॥४॥

ṣaṣṭhīsamāsaṁ manasā vicintya tvaṁ sukhī bhava||4||

shashthi-samasam — a compound in the sixth (genitive) case; manasa — in the mind; vichintya — considering; tvam — You; sukhi — happy; bhava — be.

4Understand it in Your mind as a compound in the genitive case, and be happy1."

Verse 5

तत्रोवाच प्रभुर्वाचं तथापि खिद्यते मनः।
शब्दशक्त्या करिष्यामि किमित्युक्त्वा रुरोद सः॥५॥

tatrovāca prabhurvācaṁ tathāpi khidyate manaḥ|
śabdaśaktyā kariṣyāmi kimityuktvā ruroda saḥ||5||

tatra — to that; uvacha — spoke; prabhuh — the Lord; vacham — a word; tatha api — still; khidyate — is distressed; manah — the mind; shabda-shaktya — by the power of words; karishyami — shall I do; kim — what; iti — thus; uktva — saying; ruroda — wept; sah — He.

5To this the Lord replied, "Still My mind is troubled. What am I to do with the power of words?2" And saying this, He wept.

Verse 6

तच्छ्रुत्वा व्यथिताः सर्वे कृष्णविश्लेषकातराः।
यथा भाविनि माथुरे विक्लवा व्रजसुभ्रुवः॥६॥

tacchrutvā vyathitāḥ sarve kṛṣṇaviśleṣakātarāḥ|
yathā bhāvini māthure viklavā vrajasubhruvaḥ||6||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; vyathitah — were pained; sarve — all; krishna-vishlesha-katarah — distraught at (the coming) separation from Krishna; yatha — as; bhavini — when impending; mathure — (the journey) to Mathura; viklavah — distraught; vraja-subhruvah — the fair-browed maidens of Vraja.

6Hearing this, all were stricken, distraught at the coming separation from Krishna — like the fair-browed maidens of Vraja, distraught when Krishna's journey to Mathura was at hand.

Verse 7

ततः कियद्दिने तत्र श्रीमत्केशवभारती।
न्यासिश्रेष्ठो महातेजा दीप्यमानो यथा रविः॥७॥

tataḥ kiyaddine tatra śrīmatkeśavabhāratī|
nyāsiśreṣṭho mahātejā dīpyamāno yathā raviḥ||7||

tatah — then; kiyat-dine — after some days; tatra — there; shrimat-keshava-bharati — the venerable Keshava Bharati; nyasi-shreshthah — the best of sannyasis; maha-tejah — of great power; dipyamanah — blazing; yatha — like; ravih — the sun.

7Some days later the venerable Keshava Bharati came there — the best of sannyasis, mighty and blazing like the sun.

Verse 8

पूर्वजन्मार्जितैः पुण्यैः सर्वैस्तैरागतः स्वयम्।
तत्र भाग्यवशात्कृष्णं तप्तचामीकरप्रभम्॥८॥

pūrvajanmārjitaiḥ puṇyaiḥ sarvaistairāgataḥ svayam|
tatra bhāgyavaśātkṛṣṇaṁ taptacāmīkaraprabham||8||

purva-janma-arjitaih — earned in former births; punyaih — by merits; sarvaih — all; taih — those; agatah — came; svayam — of himself; tatra — there; bhagya-vashat — by the power of good fortune; krishnam — Krishna; tapta-chamikara-prabham — shining like molten gold.

8He came of his own accord, brought by all the merits he had earned in former births. And there, by good fortune, he saw Krishna, shining like molten gold —

Verse 9

ददर्श पुण्डरीकाक्षं प्रेमविह्वलितं हरिम्।
दृष्ट्वा चानन्दपूर्णोऽसौ बभूव न्यासिसत्तमः॥९॥

dadarśa puṇḍarīkākṣaṁ premavihvalitaṁ harim|
dṛṣṭvā cānandapūrṇo'sau babhūva nyāsisattamaḥ||9||

dadarsha — saw; pundarika-aksham — the lotus-eyed; prema-vihvalitam — overwhelmed by love; harim — Hari; drishtva — seeing; cha — and; ananda-purnah — filled with bliss; asau — he; babhuva — became; nyasi-sattamah — the best of sannyasis.

9the lotus-eyed Hari, overwhelmed by love. Seeing Him, the best of sannyasis was filled with bliss.

Verse 10

न्यासीश्वरं पुरो दृष्ट्वा भगवानीश्वरः स्वयम्।
प्रेमानन्दपरिपूर्णः समुत्थाय ननाम तम्॥१०॥

nyāsīśvaraṁ puro dṛṣṭvā bhagavānīśvaraḥ svayam|
premānandaparipūrṇaḥ samutthāya nanāma tam||10||

nyasi-ishvaram — the lord of sannyasis; purah — before Him; drishtva — seeing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; ishvarah — the Lord; svayam — Himself; prema-ananda-paripurnah — filled with the bliss of love; samutthaya — rising; nanama — bowed; tam — to him.

10Bhagavan, the Lord Himself, seeing the lord of sannyasis before Him, was filled with the bliss of love; He rose and bowed down to him.

Verse 11

कृष्णप्रेमाम्बुधाराभिः परीतं तं विलोक्य सः।
प्राह तुष्टो महाबुद्धिः श्रीमत्केशवभारती॥११॥

kṛṣṇapremāmbudhārābhiḥ parītaṁ taṁ vilokya saḥ|
prāha tuṣṭo mahābuddhiḥ śrīmatkeśavabhāratī||11||

krishna-prema-ambu-dharabhih — with streams of the tears of love for Krishna; paritam — bathed; tam — Him; vilokya — seeing; sah — he; praha — said; tushtah — pleased; maha-buddhih — of great understanding; shrimat-keshava-bharati — the venerable Keshava Bharati.

11Seeing Him bathed in streams of the tears of love for Krishna, the venerable Keshava Bharati, a man of great understanding, was pleased and said:

Verse 12

त्वं शुको वाथ प्रह्लाद इति मे निश्चिता मतिः।
किंवा त्वं भगवान्साक्षादीश्वरः सर्वकारणः॥१२॥

tvaṁ śuko vātha prahlāda iti me niścitā matiḥ|
kiṁvā tvaṁ bhagavānsākṣādīśvaraḥ sarvakāraṇaḥ||12||

tvam — you; shukah — Shuka; va — or; atha — else; prahladah — Prahlada; iti — thus; me — my; nishchita — settled; matih — opinion; kim va — or else; tvam — You; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sakshat — in person; ishvarah — the Lord; sarva-karanah — the cause of all.

12"You are Shuka or Prahlada — of this I am certain. Or else You are Bhagavan Himself, the Lord, the cause of all?"

Verse 13

तच्छ्रुत्वा व्यथितो नाथः प्रशंसां स्वां महामतिः।
रुरोद द्विगुणं प्रेमवारिधारापरिप्लुतः॥१३॥

tacchrutvā vyathito nāthaḥ praśaṁsāṁ svāṁ mahāmatiḥ|
ruroda dviguṇaṁ premavāridhārāpariplutaḥ||13||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; vyathitah — pained; nathah — the Lord; prashamsam — praise; svam — of Himself; maha-matih — the great-minded; ruroda — wept; dvi-gunam — twice as much; prema-vari-dhara-pariplutah — flooded with streams of the tears of love.

13Hearing such praise of Himself, the great-minded Lord was pained, and He wept twice as much, flooded with streams of the tears of love.

Verse 14

ततः प्रोवाच तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मितो न्यासिसत्तमः।
भगवन्तं भवान्कृष्ण ईश्वरो नात्र संशयः॥१४॥

tataḥ provāca taṁ dṛṣṭvā vismito nyāsisattamaḥ|
bhagavantaṁ bhavānkṛṣṇa īśvaro nātra saṁśayaḥ||14||

tatah — then; provacha — said; tam — Him; drishtva — seeing; vismitah — astonished; nyasi-sattamah — the best of sannyasis; bhagavantam — to Bhagavan; bhavan — You; krishnah — Krishna; ishvarah — the Lord; na — no; atra — in this; samshayah — doubt.

14Then the best of sannyasis, astonished at what he saw, said to Bhagavan, "You are Krishna, the Lord — of this there is no doubt."

Verse 15

आत्मप्रशंसां महतीं श्रुत्वा वैक्लव्यमावहन्।
नत्वा तं न्यासिनां श्रेष्ठं जगाम निजमन्दिरम्॥१५॥

ātmapraśaṁsāṁ mahatīṁ śrutvā vaiklavyamāvahan|
natvā taṁ nyāsināṁ śreṣṭhaṁ jagāma nijamandiram||15||

atma-prashamsam — praise of Himself; mahatim — great; shrutva — hearing; vaiklavyam — dismay; avahan — feeling; natva — bowing; tam — to him; nyasinam — among sannyasis; shreshtham — the best; jagama — went; nija-mandiram — to His own house.

15Hearing such great praise of Himself, the Lord was dismayed; He bowed to the best of sannyasis and went to His own house.

Verse 16

न्यासं कर्तुं मनश्चक्रे त्यक्त्वा स्वगृहमृद्धिमत्।
भगवान्सर्वभूतानां पावनः श्रीनिकेतनः॥१६॥

nyāsaṁ kartuṁ manaścakre tyaktvā svagṛhamṛddhimat|
bhagavānsarvabhūtānāṁ pāvanaḥ śrīniketanaḥ||16||

nyasam — sannyasa; kartum — to take; manah chakre — resolved; tyaktva — leaving; sva-griham — His home; riddhimat — prosperous; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sarva-bhutanam — of all beings; pavanah — the purifier; shri-niketanah — the abode of Shri.

16And Bhagavan — the purifier of all beings, the abode of Shri — resolved to take sannyasa, leaving His prosperous home.

Verse 17

ततो मुकुन्दः प्रोवाच वैष्णवान्भो द्विजोत्तमाः।
पश्य नाथं जगद्योनिं यावदत्रावतिष्ठते॥१७॥

tato mukundaḥ provāca vaiṣṇavānbho dvijottamāḥ|
paśya nāthaṁ jagadyoniṁ yāvadatrāvatiṣṭhate||17||

tatah — then; mukundah — Mukunda; provacha — said; vaishnavan — to the Vaishnavas; bhoh — O; dvija-uttamah — best of the twice-born; pashya — look; natham — at the Lord; jagat-yonim — the womb of the world; yavat — while; atra — here; avatishthate — He remains.

17Then Mukunda said to the Vaishnavas, "O best of the twice-born! Look upon the Lord, the womb of the world, while He is still here:

Verse 18

गमिष्यति कियत्काले त्यक्त्वा गेहं जगद्गुरुः।
सर्वे ते व्यथिताः श्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य धीमतः॥१८॥

gamiṣyati kiyatkāle tyaktvā gehaṁ jagadguruḥ|
sarve te vyathitāḥ śrutvā vacanaṁ tasya dhīmataḥ||18||

gamishyati — will go; kiyat-kale — in a little while; tyaktva — leaving; geham — home; jagat-guruh — the teacher of the world; sarve — all; te — they; vyathitah — were pained; shrutva — hearing; vachanam — the words; tasya — of him; dhimatah — the wise.

18in a little while the teacher of the world will leave His home and go." Hearing the words of the wise Mukunda, all were stricken with grief.

Verse 19

ततः प्रोवाच भगवाञ्छ्रीवासं द्विजपुङ्गवम्।
भवतामेव प्रेमार्थं गमिष्यामि दिगन्तरम्॥१९॥

tataḥ provāca bhagavāñchrīvāsaṁ dvijapuṅgavam|
bhavatāmeva premārthaṁ gamiṣyāmi digantaram||19||

tatah — then; provacha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; shrivasam — to Srivasa; dvija-pungavam — the bull among the twice-born; bhavatam — for you; eva — indeed; prema-artham — for the sake of love; gamishyami — I shall go; dik-antaram — to distant lands.

19Then Bhagavan said to Srivasa, the bull among the twice-born, "It is for your sake, for the sake of love, that I shall go to distant lands.

Verse 20

साधुभिर्नावमारुह्य यथा गत्वा दिगन्तरम्।
अर्थमानीय बन्धुभ्यो दीयते तदहं पुनः॥२०॥

sādhubhirnāvamāruhya yathā gatvā digantaram|
arthamānīya bandhubhyo dīyate tadahaṁ punaḥ||20||

sadhubhih — by merchants; navam — a ship; aruhya — boarding; yatha — as; gatva — going; dik-antaram — to distant lands; artham — wealth; aniya — bringing back; bandhubhyah — to kinsmen; diyate — is given; tat — so; aham — I; punah — too.

20As merchants3 sail by ship to distant lands and, bringing back wealth from there, give it to their kin, so shall I:

Verse 21

दिगन्तरात्समानीय दास्यामि प्रेमसन्ततिम्।
यया सर्वसुराराध्यं श्रीकृष्णं परिपश्यसि॥२१॥

digantarātsamānīya dāsyāmi premasantatim|
yayā sarvasurārādhyaṁ śrīkṛṣṇaṁ paripaśyasi||21||

dik-antarat — from distant lands; samaniya — bringing; dasyami — I shall give; prema-santatim — an unbroken stream of love; yaya — by which; sarva-sura-aradhyam — worshipped by all the gods; shri-krishnam — Sri Krishna; paripashyasi — you will behold.

21I shall bring from distant lands and give you an unbroken stream of love, by which you will behold Sri Krishna, worshipped by all the gods."

Verse 22

पुनः प्रोवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा श्रीवासः श्रीहरिं प्रभुम्।
त्वया विरहितो नाथ कथं स्थास्यामि जीवितः॥२२॥

punaḥ provāca tacchrutvā śrīvāsaḥ śrīhariṁ prabhum|
tvayā virahito nātha kathaṁ sthāsyāmi jīvitaḥ||22||

punah — again; provacha — said; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; shrivasah — Srivasa; shri-harim — to Sri Hari; prabhum — the Lord; tvaya — by You; virahitah — forsaken; natha — O Lord; katham — how; sthasyami — shall I remain; jivitah — alive.

22Hearing this, Srivasa again spoke to the Lord, Sri Hari: "O Lord, how shall I stay alive when parted from You?"

Verse 23

तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्प्राह तव देवालये स्वयम्।
नित्यं तिष्ठामि विप्रेन्द्र न चित्ते विस्मयं कुरु॥२३॥

tacchrutvā bhagavānprāha tava devālaye svayam|
nityaṁ tiṣṭhāmi viprendra na citte vismayaṁ kuru||23||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; praha — said; tava — in your; deva-alaye — shrine; svayam — Myself; nityam — always; tishthami — I abide; vipra-indra — O king of brahmanas; na — do not; chitte — in your heart; vismayam — wonder; kuru — feel.

23Bhagavan replied, "I Myself abide always in your shrine, O king of brahmanas. Do not wonder at this."

Verse 24

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विस्मितोऽभूद्द्विजर्षभः।
ईश्वरः सर्वसंव्यापी कस्यायं वर्तते वशे॥२४॥

tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā vismito'bhūddvijarṣabhaḥ|
īśvaraḥ sarvasaṁvyāpī kasyāyaṁ vartate vaśe||24||

tasya — His; tat — those; vachanam — words; shrutva — hearing; vismitah — astonished; abhut — became; dvija-rishabhah — the bull among the twice-born; ishvarah — the Lord; sarva-samvyapi — all-pervading; kasya — whose; ayam — He; vartate — is; vashe — in the power.

24Hearing His words, the bull among the twice-born was amazed: "The Lord pervades all — whose power could ever hold Him?"

Verse 25

तत्र श्रीहरिदासेन सार्धं सायं गतो हरिः।
मुरारिवेश्म कारुण्यात्सोऽभ्यगच्छद्धरेः पदम्॥२५॥

tatra śrīharidāsena sārdhaṁ sāyaṁ gato hariḥ|
murāriveśma kāruṇyātso'bhyagacchaddhareḥ padam||25||

tatra — then; shri-haridasena sardham — together with Sri Haridasa; sayam — in the evening; gatah — went; harih — Hari; murari-veshma — to Murari's house; karunyat — out of compassion; sah — he (Murari); abhyagachchhat — approached; hareh — Hari's; padam — feet.

25Then, in the evening, Hari in His compassion came with Sri Haridasa to Murari's house, and Murari fell at Hari's feet.

Verse 26

नत्वासनमुपानीय दत्त्वा सन्तुष्टमानसः।
हरिदासं प्रणम्याथ सन्निकर्षे स्थितः स्वयम्॥२६॥

natvāsanamupānīya dattvā santuṣṭamānasaḥ|
haridāsaṁ praṇamyātha sannikarṣe sthitaḥ svayam||26||

natva — bowing; asanam — a seat; upaniya — bringing; dattva — offering; santushta-manasah — glad at heart; haridasam — to Haridasa; pranamya — bowing; atha — then; sannikarshe — nearby; sthitah — stood; svayam — himself.

26Having bowed, glad at heart he brought and offered Him a seat; then he bowed to Haridasa and himself stood close by.

Verse 27

तमुवाच दयाम्भोधिर्मुरारिं शृणु मद्वचः।
यदुदास्से सदा नित्यं तदित्थं कुरु मद्वचः॥२७॥

tamuvāca dayāmbhodhirmurāriṁ śṛṇu madvacaḥ|
yadudāsse sadā nityaṁ taditthaṁ kuru madvacaḥ||27||

tam — to him; uvacha — said; daya-ambhodhih — the ocean of mercy; murarim — to Murari; shrinu — hear; mat-vachah — My word; yat — that to which; udasse — you are indifferent; sada nityam — always; tat — that; ittham — thus; kuru — do; mat-vachah — (by) My word.

27And the ocean of mercy said to Murari, "Hear My word: that to which you have always been indifferent, do from now on as I tell you4.

Verse 28

सावधानेन भवता श्रोतव्यं वचनं मम।
उपदेशं ददाम्यद्य तव तत्सम्प्रधार्यताम्॥२८॥

sāvadhānena bhavatā śrotavyaṁ vacanaṁ mama|
upadeśaṁ dadāmyadya tava tatsampradhāryatām||28||

savadhanena — attentive; bhavata — by you; shrotavyam — is to be heard; vachanam — word; mama — My; upadesham — instruction; dadami — I give; adya — today; tava — to you; tat — it; sampradharyatam — let it be firmly kept in mind.

28Listen to Me attentively: today I give you an instruction — keep it firmly in mind.

Verse 29

अद्वैताचार्यवर्योऽसौ महान्वै सद्गुणाश्रयः।
ईश्वरांशोऽस्य सेवां च कुरु यत्नेन सादरम्॥२९॥

advaitācāryavaryo'sau mahānvai sadguṇāśrayaḥ|
īśvarāṁśo'sya sevāṁ ca kuru yatnena sādaram||29||

advaita-acharya-varyah — the excellent Advaita Acharya; asau — this; mahan — great; vai — truly; sat-guna-ashrayah — the abode of virtues; ishvara-amshah — a portion of the Lord; asya — to him; sevam — service; cha — and; kuru — render; yatnena — with care; sa-adaram — with reverence.

29The excellent Advaita Acharya is truly great: He is the abode of virtues, a portion of the Lord5. Serve Him with care and reverence.

Verse 30

इत्येवं ज्ञापितो गुह्यो मया त्वत्सुखसिद्धये।
इत्युक्त्वा स ययौ देवः स्वां पुरीं भक्तवत्सलः॥३०॥

ityevaṁ jñāpito guhyo mayā tvatsukhasiddhaye|
ityuktvā sa yayau devaḥ svāṁ purīṁ bhaktavatsalaḥ||30||

iti evam — thus; jnapitah — has been made known; guhyah — the secret (instruction); maya — by Me; tvat-sukha-siddhaye — for your happiness; iti — thus; uktva — saying; sah — He; yayau — went; devah — the Lord; svam — to His own; purim — town (home); bhakta-vatsalah — loving to His devotees.

30Thus I have disclosed this secret instruction to you for your happiness." Having said this, the Lord, so loving to His devotees, went home.

Verse 31

अथापरदिने गत्वा कण्टकग्राममुत्तमम्।
सन्न्यासं कृतवान्कृष्णः श्रीमत्केशवभारतीम्॥३१॥

athāparadine gatvā kaṇṭakagrāmamuttamam|
sannyāsaṁ kṛtavānkṛṣṇaḥ śrīmatkeśavabhāratīm||31||

atha — then; apara-dine — on the next day; gatva — going; kantaka-gramam — to the village of Kantaka; uttamam — excellent; sannyasam — sannyasa; kritavan — took; krishnah — Krishna; shrimat-keshava-bharatim — the venerable Keshava Bharati.

31And on the next day Krishna went to the fine village of Kantaka6 and took sannyasa,

Verse 32

कृतार्थयन्गुरुं कृत्वा तं ब्रह्मपारगोत्तमम्॥३२॥

kṛtārthayanguruṁ kṛtvā taṁ brahmapāragottamam||32||

kritarthayan — blessing; gurum — guru; kritva — making; tam — him; brahma-paraga-uttamam — the best of those who have reached the far shore of Brahman.

32making the venerable Keshava Bharati, the best of those who have reached the far shore of Brahman, His guru, and so fulfilling his life.

Verse 33

इति हरेश्चरितं संशृणोति यः
सपदि पापगणं परिहाय सः।
विशति पादतले नृहरेर्लभे-
दतुलभक्तिमसङ्गमनार्यतः॥३३॥

iti hareścaritaṁ saṁśṛṇoti yaḥ
sapadi pāpagaṇaṁ parihāya saḥ|
viśati pādatale nṛharerlabhe-
datulabhaktimasaṅgamanāryataḥ||33||

iti — thus; hareh — of Hari; charitam — the deeds; samshrinoti — hears; yah — who; sapadi — at once; papa-ganam — the host of sins; parihaya — casting off; sah — he; vishati — enters; pada-tale — at the soles of the feet; nrihareh — of Nrihari; labhet — will gain; atula-bhaktim — incomparable devotion; asangam — detachment; anaryatah — from the ignoble.

33Whoever thus hears the deeds of Hari at once casts off the host of his sins and comes to the soles of Nrihari's feet; he will gain incomparable devotion and freedom from attachment to all that is ignoble.

Thus ends the eighteenth sarga, "The Prelude to Sannyasa" (Sannyasa-sutra), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita." Thus the second prakrama is complete.

✦

Notes

  1. Murari suggests interpreting the sannyasa mantra, which speaks of identity with Brahman, through the genitive case: not "I am He" but "I am His," that is, the Lord's servant. This is how the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition understands the great sayings of the Upanishads.
  2. That is, skilful interpretation does not console the Lord: in the mood of a devotee He grieves that the sannyasa mantra, by its very sound, speaks of identity with Brahman.
  3. The word sadhu here, as commonly in Bengal, means a merchant engaged in overseas trade.
  4. The sense is unfolded in v. 29: the Lord bids Murari to serve Advaita Acharya diligently. It may also be understood as "you are always detached — so carry out My word."
  5. Cf. 2.16, the note to v. 4: "portion" (amsha) does not diminish Advaita — according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching He is Maha-Vishnu Himself (together with Sadashiva), non-different from the Lord.
  6. Kantaka (Kantakanagara) is present-day Katwa on the bank of the Ganga.
